newsitem.title: ITALY: Food superpowers solve dinner riddle at summit.
newsitem.headline: Food superpowers solve dinner riddle at summit.

text.p: Representatives of the world's two food superpowers answered the question tormenting the assembled media at a food summit on Thursday -- what were leaders eating after a day debating global hunger?

The answer, in the case of U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and European Union farm chief Franz Fischler who dined together at a Rome hotel on Thursday night, was a four-course menu of fish and pasta washed down with Sauvignon.
However there was a nod at moderation.
The starter, on a printed menu seen by Reuters, was listed as "ricciola all'aceto balsamico" -- a green leaf in balsamic vinegar recommended by Italians for days of fasting.

Next, the two men and their aides ate "linguine", or flat spaghetti, tossed in anchovy and fresh tomato sauce. For a main course they had baked fish and potatoes and then rounded off their working dinner with a traditional Italian sorbet.
"It was excellent -- the conversation, the meal, and my host was very hospitable," Glickman said afterwards.
The meal was carried in by waiters from a nearby restaurant because the historic hotel where Fischler was staying for the summit lacked catering facilities.
